title: Lizzie Borden Back in the Spotlight with Netflix Series
seoTitle: Lizzie Borden Back in the Spotlight with Netflix Series
subtitle: The release of "Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story" reignites debate about the 1892 case
excerpt: Ryan Murphy's series premiere about Lizzie Borden stirred Netflix audiences, bringing the mystery surrounding the 1892 murders back into discussion.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Last week, Netflix released the third season of its true crime anthology, featuring "Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story." The title topped the list of English-language series, accumulating over 12 million views in its first four days, which explains the sudden interest in searches for Lizzie Borden.

What Brings Lizzie Borden into the Spotlight

The episode is part of Ryan Murphy's cinematic universe, which has previously explored famous murderers. By presenting the story of the 32-year-old woman accused of the murders of her father, Andrew Borden, and stepmother, Abby Borden, the production rekindled fascination with a case that, despite being over a century old, still raises questions.

How the Facts Were Recorded in 1892

On August 4, 1892, 70-year-old Andrew and 64-year-old Abby were found bludgeoned in their Fall River home. The weapon identified by investigators was a small axe found in the basement. Lizzie, who was in the house at the time of the crimes, became the prime suspect, primarily due to her contentious relationship with her stepmother.

The Trial and Acquittal

An all-male jury deliberated for just over an hour before declaring Lizzie innocent, despite the evidence pointing to her. The decision reflected, according to contemporary accounts, the difficulty of accepting that a wealthy, educated woman could commit such violent acts.

Recent Revisions of the Case

Current research indicates that the weapon was not an axe, but a small iron hatchet, and that Abby was struck fewer than twelve times, although the brutality remains evident. Forensic science experts emphasize that, with modern resources, it would be possible to detect traces of blood on Lizzie's clothes, something that did not occur in the original investigation.

The Current State of the Lizzie Borden House

The 180-year-old residence, located on Second Street, has been restored and operates as a museum and bed and breakfast. The site displays black-and-white photographs of the crime scene, including images of Abby's body in the room where the article's author spent the night. The atmosphere still attracts curious visitors who wish to experience the environment where the murders occurred.

Why the Case Still Intrigue

The combination of a violent crime, a controversial trial, and the lack of conclusive evidence keeps Lizzie Borden alive in popular culture, inspiring books, films, and even a children's rhyme. The release of the Netflix series brings these questions to the forefront again, allowing new generations to question the circumstances surrounding the case.

With information from Deadline, CBS News.
